images.title: Change a value, the formula updates
images.purpose: Before and after: changing 27 to 30 makes =AVERAGE(B7:D7) change from 30 to 31 by itself.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two identical one row strips of four cells stacked one above the other, with a formula tag on the right.
images.exact_structure: Two identical rows of 4 cells each, one above the other. In each row the first 3 cells are outlined in teal (#0072B2) as one range and the 4th cell, the result, is outlined in reddish purple (#CC79A7). Top row: 27, 29, 34 and result 30. Bottom row: 30, 29, 34 and result 31; the first cell, 30, is filled light amber (#E69F00) to show it was changed, and the result 31 is bold. One short dark arrow points down from the top row to the bottom row. A single tag to the right of the two result cells reads =AVERAGE(B7:D7). No column or row headers, no other text.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A formula recalculates by itself when a value in its range changes.
images.description: Before and after: changing 27 to 30 makes =AVERAGE(B7:D7) change from 30 to 31 by itself.
images.context: Gowri's marks 27, 29, 34 average 30; with 27 changed to 30 the average is 93 divided by 3, 31.
images.teaching_notes: The bottom row shows the values 30, 29, 34 and 31; the label 30 is reused for the changed cell.

image_decisions.why: The practice tool's key move, edit a cell and watch the result update, shown in its simplest state.
